title: Second Life UX, onboarding, retention, governance and public perception
summary: Live-search revision of the Second Life UX/onboarding/governance brief, using all 20 searches (fetching blocked; facts rest on search extracts). Linden Lab's own stated retention was ~10% at 90 days (Jan 2007, "unchanged over 12 months"); Wired (Frank Rose, July 2007) reported >85% of avatars abandoned and ~1M of 7M logged in within 30 days; peak concurrency hit an all-time 88,000 in 2009 and 2008 U2U transactions were US$361M. The empty-world problem is arithmetic: 76,000 peak avatars over ~30,000 regions then, and a 32,000 median over 26,663 regions in late 2025 (third-party tracker; Linden publishes no official numbers). Altberg named viewer complexity and hardware as the second-login blocker; Firestorm became the dominant viewer. Governance followed a repeated arc of unilateral decree then partial reversal: Openspace pricing (Oct-Nov 2008), Zindra adult segregation (announced 12 Mar 2009, opened 15 Jun 2009 with 157 regions, ~850 move tickets), the 30% layoffs (9 Jun 2010) and CEO exit (24 Jun 2010), the education discount removal (1 Jan 2011, restored 2013), and the August 2013 ToS Section 2.3 that caused Renderosity/CG Textures bans until the July 2014 revision. Corporate presence (Reuters Oct 2006-Nov 2008, Sweden's embassy 30 May 2007, IBM's 1,850-avatar Italian strike 27 Sep 2007) ended in the 2007 press backlash. The durable things were resident-owned: the CDS democracy (since 21 Sep 2004, still six regions), Virtual Ability (first Linden Prize 2009), and the resident-run SL9B (2012). Corrections to the prior draft: retention figure was 90-day not 30-day; Homestead pricing was phased $75->$95->$125, not a climb-down; Basic-mode withdrawal and 400k signups/month unverified.
design_implications: Instrument and publish first-hour, 7/30/90-day retention from launch; define first-hour success as 'met a person or joined a group', since SL's 10%-at-90-days figure never moved across a decade of orientation redesigns.

Abandon fixed region sharding in favour of density management so newcomers always land where people and a host are; SL's emptiness was arithmetic (76k peak avatars over ~30k regions in 2008; 32k median over 26,663 regions in 2025).
Ship separate consumer and creator/pro interfaces over one world and never let incumbents veto the newcomer client; expect and bless a third-party client ecosystem early (Firestorm lesson).
Keep the hardware floor low with a thin/streaming client and instant first render; Linden's CEO named viewer complexity and client performance as the top second-login blocker.
Provide purpose without quests: hosted scheduled activities and apprenticeship routes into communities (music, building, education, disability support), which were SL's durable retention engines.

Adopt constitutional change control: a published charter, notice periods and a resident assembly with bounded but real powers over mainland rules, pricing and ToS, so Openspace (2008), education pricing (2010), Zindra (2009) and ToS (2013)-style shocks cannot happen by blog post.
Grant content rights to creators by default with a narrow operating licence, and enforce permissions server-side with provenance, so neither a CopyBot nor a ToS rewrite can trigger a creator strike.
Design maturity zoning and age assurance in from day one with first-class segregated adult space, rather than a forced relocation of ~850 parcels later.
Set financial rules up front (no unregulated interest-bearing products; clear currency redemption terms) rather than banning gambling and banks after a Ginko-scale collapse.
Guarantee pricing stability for institutional communities (education, non-profit, disability) and sell brands outcomes (hosts, events, measured traffic) rather than land.
open_questions: Has Linden Lab ever published first-hour or 30-day retention figures (as opposed to the 90-day ~10% figure), and did Altberg's 2014-2018 town halls give numbers?
Was Viewer 2 'Basic mode' actually withdrawn, when, and with what retention evidence? (Search found only its 2011 introduction and feature additions.)
Did Homestead pricing in fact step to US$125 in July 2009, or was the second increase cancelled after further protest?
What share of the ~850 Zindra move tickets were relocations versus closures, and how many regions did Zindra reach after the July 2009 expansion?
What is Linden Lab's current official MAU (last stated ~900,000 in 2015 versus a reported ~500,000 plateau), and what are the 2020 Oberwager acquisition and 2022 Rosedale-return details (unsearched)?
Did Renderosity and CG Textures lift their asset bans after the July 2014 Section 2.3 revision?
How many of the 2011 education departures returned after the 2013 discount restoration?
What are Linden's revenue splits (tier vs Marketplace vs LindeX fees) across 2007-2025?
Is the '400,000 sign-ups per month' (Humble, 2013) figure real, and what is the current sign-up rate against the ~69M account total?

claims.claim: Linden Lab stated in January 2007 that new-user retention to 90 days was about 10% and had remained roughly unchanged over the prior 12 months (Massively, via Andrew Chen).

Wired's July 2007 Frank Rose cover story reported that more than 85% of avatars created had been abandoned; ~7M avatars, ~4M distinct individuals per Linden, ~1M logged in during the previous 30 days; Sears' traffic score was 281 and Coke's Virtual Thirst pavilion 27.

Linden Lab's 2008 metrics: nearly 400M user hours (+61%), Q4 2008 peak concurrency 76,000, US$361M user-to-user transactions; the all-time peak concurrency was 88,000 (2009), with Q3 2009 at >77,000 after a bot-restriction policy.
On 9 June 2010 Linden Lab laid off about 30% of its 300+ staff and merged product and engineering; CEO Mark Kingdon stepped down 24 June 2010 with Rosedale as interim CEO.

The August 2013 ToS Section 2.3 revision led Renderosity and CG Textures to ban use of their assets in Second Life; Linden revised 2.3 in July 2014 to limit rights to use 'inworld or otherwise on the Service' and require affirmative user action for sale/sublicensing.

Adult-content segregation was announced 12 March 2009; Zindra (built as 'Ursula') opened 15 June 2009 with Viewer 1.23 and age verification, with an initial 157 regions, ~850 move tickets filed 29 Jun-24 Jul 2009, and a 15 September 2009 relocation deadline.

Reuters opened its Second Life bureau in early October 2006 (Adam Pasick, 'Adam Reuters') and closed it in November 2008; Sweden's Second House of Sweden opened 30 May 2007 (cost 400,000 SEK, ~US$57,000), days after the Maldives' first virtual embassy.
Linden ended the 50% education/non-profit discount effective 1 January 2011 (announced late 2010, doubling region costs) and restored it in 2013; the move drove institutions toward OpenSim.

The Confederation of Democratic Simulators began 21 September 2004 as the Neualtenburg Project, has a three-person Executive, a five-member Representative Assembly and a five-member Scientific Council, ties citizenship to land ownership, and still operates (land store lists six regions).

In 2025 (third-party grid tracker) Second Life's peak concurrency was 49,798 (24 March 2025), the mid-December daily median was ~32,000-35,000, and there were 26,663 regions on 10 August 2025 (about 9,033 Linden-owned, down ~800 during the year); registered accounts ~68.98M.
